families.purpose: Cross-cutting quality concerns a piece of work carries, independent of which subsystem it changes.
families.lifecycle: Applied while the concern applies and removed when it stops; not a triage state and not a classification axis.

values.name: sec
values.description: Security concern

values.name: a11y
values.description: Accessibility concern

values.name: perf
values.description: Performance concern

values.name: tech-debt
values.description: Technical debt

values.name: i18n
values.description: Internationalization

values.name: l10n
values.description: Localization

families.purpose: Where the work came from: a customer asked for it, or an AI agent authored it.
families.lifecycle: Never removed. Provenance is a historical fact about how the issue came to exist, not a state that can stop being true.

values.name: customer-request
values.description: Requested by a customer

values.name: ai-generated
values.description: Created or authored by an AI agent

families.purpose: Transient process states: what the issue is currently waiting on before it can move.
families.lifecycle: Transient — removed as soon as the state it names no longer holds.

values.name: needs-triage
values.description: Awaiting triage
values.lifecycle: Added freely; removed only when classification is complete.

values.name: needs-requirements
values.description: Requirements not yet defined

values.name: blocked
values.description: Blocked by a non-issue dependency (reason in a comment)

values.name: waiting
values.description: Waiting on an external party

values.name: needs-decision
values.description: Needs a decision before it can proceed

values.name: needs-response
values.description: Awaiting a response

values.name: needs-communication
values.description: An update needs to be communicated out

families.purpose: Stack slice the change lands in. Mirrors the Layer project field's option list, with no per-issue sync.
families.lifecycle: Set at triage and corrected as scope changes; at most one per issue.

values.name: ui
values.description: Components, styling, interaction, tokens, a11y. No data change

values.name: logic
values.description: Business rules, handlers, calculation

values.name: data
values.description: Schema, indexes, validators, migrations

values.name: integration
values.description: External boundary: webhooks, API clients, credentials

families.purpose: Product capability (problem space) the work belongs to. Mirrors the Domain project field's option list.
families.lifecycle: Set at triage and corrected as scope changes; at most one per issue.

values.name: auth
values.description: Authentication and authorization

values.name: billing
values.description: Billing and payments

values.name: platform
values.description: CI, build, test infra, and tooling in this repo

families.purpose: Which round-cap tier in .devflow.toml an agent works the issue under (AGENTS.md, "Round caps are resolved, not stated here").
families.lifecycle: Applied by a human before work starts. An agent reads it and is never a writer of it — never on itself.

values.name: light
values.description: Dev Loop caps: trivial, low-blast-radius change

values.name: standard
values.description: Dev Loop caps: the default budget

values.name: deep
values.description: Dev Loop caps: security, migrations, irreversible paths

families.purpose: Advisory routing: which agent family should implement the issue. Routes nothing by itself and is never arming.
families.lifecycle: Set at triage and replaced when routing changes; survives the work, unlike a claim.

families.purpose: Live ownership: which agent family is working the issue right now, written by the agent itself.
families.lifecycle: Added when an agent claims the issue and released when it wraps up or abandons the work.

families.purpose: Foreman's arming selectors and its own workflow protocol. The only arming namespace: upstream reads any unrecognized value here as a backend selector.
families.lifecycle: Applied by hand as an input foreman reads. Removal is per value, below — foreman never clears its own inputs.

values.name: approved
values.description: Arm with the repo default backend
values.lifecycle: Applied to arm the issue; stays on it. The adapter selectors composed into this family behave the same way.

values.name: hold
values.description: Exclude from foreman dispatch (always wins)
values.lifecycle: Applied to exclude the issue, removed by a human to re-include it.

values.name: satisfied
values.description: Human override: treat this dependency as satisfied
values.lifecycle: Applied per dependency decision and left in place as the record of that decision.

values.name: external
values.description: External dependency: satisfied when closed as completed
values.lifecycle: Applied per dependency decision and left in place as the record of that decision.

values.name: dispatched
values.description: Foreman is working this issue; its draft PR carries the same label
values.lifecycle: Written by foreman on dispatch and superseded by foreman:ready-for-review.

values.name: ready-for-review
values.description: Foreman's draft passed its readiness gate and is handed to a human
values.lifecycle: Written by foreman when it promotes its draft; cleared by the human who merges or closes it.

families.purpose: Advisory model routing: which model stratum a consumer should prefer. Inert on its own — nothing invokes a model because the label exists.
families.lifecycle: Set at triage. Two present resolve strongest-wins, so a conflict can only ever buy more capability.

values.name: local
values.description: Model tier: self-hosted endpoint first; may escalate to economy

values.name: economy
values.description: Model tier: cheapest qualified hosted model first; escalation allowed

values.name: standard
values.description: Model tier: reliable general-purpose coding model first

values.name: frontier
values.description: Model tier: opus-class heavyweights; no warm-up on weaker models

values.name: apex
values.description: Model tier: mythos-class leading edge (fable, sol)

values.name: adaptive
values.description: Model tier: cheap preflight classifies, then chooses or escalates

families.purpose: Advisory execution topology: how an agent should work the issue. Conflicts resolve by the configured method rank, most human oversight first.
families.lifecycle: Set at triage and advisory only; a consumer with no method configuration ignores it.

values.name: oneshot
values.description: Execution: single agent, no separate plan phase

values.name: plan
values.description: Execution: agent plans then implements; no human plan gate

values.name: plan-approved
values.description: Execution: plan requires human approval before implementation

values.name: orchestrate
values.description: Execution: conductor session drives subagents, possibly across related issues

values.name: council
values.description: Execution: N independent implementations; judged, best or synthesis wins

values.name: human-led
values.description: Execution: human owns central decisions; AI does bounded pieces

families.purpose: Codebase subsystem (solution space) the work touches. Area is where the change lands, domain is the capability it serves.
families.lifecycle: Set at triage and corrected as scope changes; at most one per issue.

values.name: build
values.description: Build system and packaging

values.name: ci
values.description: GitHub Actions workflows and CI plumbing

values.name: deps
values.description: Dependency management and pins

values.name: docs
values.description: Documentation content and structure

values.name: skills
values.description: Agent skills (ai/skills) and their packaging

families.purpose: Kind of work, for repos with no native issue Type. Deliberately not a type:* family — that prefix is foreman's conventional-commit override.
families.lifecycle: At most one per issue; the axis is exclusive. Nothing applies one — the issue forms set no label, so triage does. Where an org has native Type, that is authoritative and these are unused.

values.name: task
values.description: General work: maintenance, chores, cleanup

values.name: research
values.description: Produces a decision or written answer, not a code change

families.purpose: release-please's bookkeeping on the rolling release PR. Documented so triage recognizes it; the colon-space in each name is release-please's own spelling.
families.lifecycle: Created and moved by release-please on its own release PR; never applied, removed, or provisioned by hand.

values.name: autorelease: pending
values.description: release-please: the release PR is open and not yet merged

values.name: autorelease: tagged
values.description: release-please: the merged release has been tagged
